pairs.question: Quid proderit libatio idolo?
pairs.derivation: Single verse (CAPUT 30, v.19) with the verse-number scaffolding '19' stripped. The author poses the rhetorical question 'quid proderit libatio idolo' and answers it in the same breath with the causal clause 'nec enim manducat nec odorabitur' (for it neither eats nor smells), explaining why the offering profits nothing. Split at the question's natural break: '?' added to the question; the answering clause kept whole. The following v.20 ('sic qui effugatur a Domino...') begins a fresh simile and is excluded.

pairs.question: Quare dies diem superat et iterum lux lucem et annus annum a sole?
pairs.answer: A Domini scientia separati sunt facto sole et praeceptum custodiente.
pairs.derivation: CAPUT 33, vv.7-8, with verse-number scaffolding ('7','8') stripped. v.7 is the explicit interrogative 'quare dies diem superat...' (why does one day surpass another...). v.8 directly answers: by the Lord's knowledge they were distinguished. Answer window stops at the end of v.8's operative sentence; v.9 onward ('et inmutavit tempora et dies festos...') digresses into feast-days and is cut. First word capitalized, '?' added to the question; no '...' ellipsis, no reordering.
